data.text:
The Day We Stopped Being Tired

I woke at 2 a.m.—not from a dream, but from sheer exhaustion. Slept at 10 p.m. after a long day at the hospital, capped by a two-hour crawl through Manila traffic. A punishment for service, it seems.

Dinner was a soft landing: family gathered, and a video call with Marge and our Lily Bear in the UK. That moment—simple, sacred—reminded me why I keep showing up.

By 6 a.m., I was on air for a radio interview, speaking on the Department of Health’s curious stance: no zero balance billing… for traffic violators. Yes, even our metaphors are tired.

Then came the treadmill. I watched an old John Grisham thriller, The Client, with Tommy Lee Jones and Susan Sarandon—two hours of courtroom drama and quiet grit.

Then the bed. Then two hours of unplanned sleep. My body was tired. But not as tired as Speaker Martin Romualdez claims to be.

Tired? Of what, exactly?
Tired of power?
Tired of defending the indefensible?
Tired of long, drawn-out discussions about whether to let go of a title that no longer inspires trust?

Or perhaps tired of living a life padded by billions, Forbes Park mansions, private jets, and lawmakers who swarm like bees—not for honey, but for proximity to power. Tired of being respected for position, not principle.

Today, I’m wearing business casual—patterned after Roger Federer. A quiet nod to grace under pressure. No jet. No convoy. Just me, a cup of coffee, and a clinic full of hope.

I’m not tired. I’m excited.

Because today, kindred spirits—ordinary citizens, reformists, dreamers—have signified their readiness to fight corruption and abuse. Today is about hope. About change. About the possibility of a new Congress leadership that might finally steer us toward budget reform, legislative integrity, and an end to the quiet rot that’s been eating away at our democracy.

We’re nearing a tipping point. And if those in power don’t act today, the people will. They’re perked up. They’re fed up.

So I wait. With coffee in hand. With faith in the Filipino spirit. With love for Simmy and Lily Bear, and for every child who deserves a country that fights for their future.

If change doesn’t come today, it will come tomorrow.
Because we are no longer tired.
We are awake.

Dr. Tony Leachon 

#HealthWithHonor
#RelentlessForChange
